extracted.intended_audience: open-source contributors and project maintainers using GitHub (authors and reviewers of pull requests)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, actionable guidance for creating, responding to, reviewing, and merging GitHub pull requests for open-source projects, including setup, branching, testing, documentation, review workflow, and merge policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign up for a GitHub account
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign up for a GitHub account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite for contributing; simple setup step included in preliminaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install Git
rubrics_metrics.description: Install Git locally so you can clone repositories and run git commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prerequisite for local development and interacting with forks/branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fork the project
rubrics_metrics.description: Fork the project (use the “Fork” button) to make your own copy of the repository on GitHub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original project is 'upstream'; your copy is a 'fork'. Work in your fork and create PRs from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable continuous integration on your fork
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable the same continuous integration that upstream uses on your fork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions provided for Azure Pipelines, CircleCI, GitHub Workflows, and Travis CI. Ensures CI runs on your pushes and PRs so tests run automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clone your fork locally and add upstream remote
rubrics_metrics.description: Clone your fork locally and create a git remote named 'upstream' referring to the original repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example git clone commands provided; run 'git remote add upstream https://github.com/OTHERUSER/REPONAME.git' and 'git fetch upstream'. Compile and run tests as a sanity check using project README instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start work on a new branch for each unit of work
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting a unit of work (bug fix or feature), create a branch; each branch should represent a logical unit of work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'git switch -c MYBRANCHNAME' (or older 'git checkout -b') and remember which branch is current. Avoid making changes to the wrong branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use descriptive, readable branch names
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose descriptive, readable branch names (e.g., 'unicode-support' or 'fix-issue-22').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readable names make intent clear to reviewers and maintainers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not work on your fork's main branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not work on the main branch in your fork; keep it identical to upstream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working on main causes spurious merge commits; instead create a new branch for each PR. If main is contaminated, re-forking is suggested over advanced git commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write tests first that fail, then implement the fix
rubrics_metrics.description: Before implementing changes, write tests that currently fail but will pass once the bug is fixed or feature implemented; commit and push the tests first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run tests locally to confirm they fail, commit tests, push, verify CI runs and shows the failure, then implement code and make tests pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit logical chunks frequently
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit your work in logical chunks as you go.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent, logically separated commits make the change history more helpful. However, history rewrites are discouraged (see avoid rebasing/amending).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be done only when tests pass and documentation is updated
rubrics_metrics.description: Being done requires at least: testing (tests written and passing locally and in CI), documentation (update procedures, user manual, changelog if appropriate), and completeness (fix all places the problem manifests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check all three before creating a pull request. Completeness includes searching for similar code and fixing all occurrences at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodically pull upstream into your branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate changes from upstream into your branch frequently rather than all at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commands like 'git pull upstream BRANCHNAME' or pull from the upstream URL. If any effect occurs: resolve merge conflicts, check tests locally, push changes, and check CI tests again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide changes into logical units; each PR should be single-concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Each pull request should be a single, logical unit of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate unrelated changes (bug fixes, refactorings, docs) into different branches/PRs; this makes reviews faster, test failures easier to understand, and interactions clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a branch contains multiple distinct changes, split them into new branches and PRs
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple distinct changes exist in a branch, create new branches for each distinct change and open separate PRs for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You don't need to undo changes in the combined branch: copy relevant changes into the new branches, open PRs, and pull those branches into the combined branch as needed so it becomes single-concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update your branch from upstream before creating a pull request
rubrics_metrics.description: Before creating a pull request, update your branch from upstream and ensure it passes all tests locally and in CI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids merge conflicts and ensures your change integrates cleanly with recent upstream work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the diff and do not include unrelated or gratuitous changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a PR, review the shown changes and ensure there are no changes not related to the main topic of the branch (or gratuitous whitespace/formatting changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unrelated changes are present, undo them in your working copy, commit, and create a smaller, cleaner PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a descriptive title and, when appropriate, an explanatory paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a descriptive title appropriate as a commit message and sometimes include a paragraph explaining what you have done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PR title becomes the default squash commit first line; a clear PR description is recommended and later used when squashing and merging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link issues or include 'fixes #NNN' to auto-close issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If the PR fixes issues, include 'fixes #NNN' in the descriptive paragraph or use the 'linked issues' UI to link the PR to issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either method links the PR to the issue and automatically closes it when the PR is accepted. Putting 'fixes #NNN' in the title does not always work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable 'Allow edits from maintainers'
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the 'Allow edits from maintainers' checkbox is enabled when creating the PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows maintainers to make minor edits directly on your branch to facilitate integration and fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make code self-explanatory; put necessary info in code/comments, not PR thread
rubrics_metrics.description: Make your code self-explanatory; avoid writing code comments in your own pull request and write very little in the introductory PR comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information needed by a programmer reading the source should be in a code comment or documentation so it remains visible to future readers after merge. Also applies to answering reviewers' questions: improve code/docs rather than only replying in the PR thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use private pull requests for early feedback (rare)
rubrics_metrics.description: For feedback before you're ready to merge into a different fork, create a pull request between two branches of your fork (private PR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a temporary target branch (e.g., 'codeReviewTargetTemporary') kept up-to-date with the intended merge target; create PR merging your working branch into that temporary branch and assign someone to review; discard the temporary branch afterward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflows for reviewing already-pushed code (rare)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want a review of already-pushed code or a holistic review of a component, use one of two workarounds because GitHub's PRs don't support this workflow well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: create a new empty branch and PR main into it (never merge), or reviewer creates a 'review' branch cloned from main, both edit it adding TODO comments until resolved, then merge into main.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to review feedback by changing code, committing, and pushing (don't reply 'Done')
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to feedback by making changes in your working copy, committing them, and pushing when tests pass; don't clutter review threads with terse replies like 'Done' or 'I did that'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you agree with a comment and implement it, mark it resolved. Only engage in discussion when needed (followups or disagreements). Improve docs/code rather than just replying in the review system so future readers benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not force-push (avoid 'git push -f')
rubrics_metrics.description: Never force a push, as it causes loss of code review comments GitHub attached to commits and can cause merge conflicts for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Force-pushing is bad practice; preserve commit history and the association of comments to commits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be careful when pushing changes that alter lines with review comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pushing changes (e.g., indentation) that change a line without addressing all related comments, because GitHub will mark comments as out of date or hide them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you change a line near a review comment, the review comment may no longer be shown by default; try not to hide unresolved discussion by incidental edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly request re-review after addressing feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: After addressing all review feedback, explicitly request a re-review; do not assume the reviewer will know when you are done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ways to request re-review: add the person as a reviewer on the PR page, assign the PR to them via 'Assignees', or write a comment in the PR conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't reply to PR comments by email; reply on GitHub
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not reply to PR notification emails; instead respond on the GitHub webpage referenced by the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replying by email can bloat messages with quoted text and may not associate the response with the correct GitHub thread.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rebasing, amending commits, or rewriting branch history
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't rebase, amend commits, or otherwise change existing version control history for the branch used for the PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are confusing and error-prone, can corrupt the pull request, and are unnecessary because the repo will squash-and-merge; focus on differences from upstream instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: When merging: squash-and-merge (squash, don't just merge)
rubrics_metrics.description: When merging a PR, select 'Squash and merge' to keep the main branch history clean so each logical change is one commit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A PR is a single conceptual change; squashing yields a linear history, avoids many tiny commits in main, and ensures each main commit passes tests. Repository owners can disable merge commits and rebase merging to enforce this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit the squash commit message to a useful message
rubrics_metrics.description: When squashing and merging, edit the commit message: use the PR's description and remove concatenated commit messages that are not useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove commit message clutter and '[ci skip]' tokens that could prevent CI actions. Use the initial PR description (first comment) as the basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository merge settings: disable merge commits and rebase merging; enable auto-delete head branches
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository owners can prevent incorrect merges by disabling 'Allow merge commits' and 'Allow rebase merging' and enabling 'Automatically delete head branches'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These settings encourage squash-and-merge and remove merged branches automatically to reduce clutter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider automated tool feedback seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: If an automated tool (e.g., CodeRabbit or Copilot) gives code review feedback, consider each comment and make changes if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After making changes suggested by automated tools, click 'resolve comment' where applicable. Treat automated suggestions like human review comments but apply judgement.
